# Guide to the data files in the `kuky_data` folder

I will list the files in the order of coming into existence. 

-   `argumentative.json`: from KUKY 1.0 on Lindat

- `ArgM_spans_nested_links.rds`: conversion to a data frame. All spans, but links are nested lists in columns. An important concept here is `owner`: This is the annotator. Some documents have parallel annotation by several annotators (to check the inter-annotator agreement). I keep all annotations, but whenever documents are to be treated individually, I will treat each document-owner pair as a separate document. 

- `argm.rds`: all spans from json, uncleaned but ArgM only. 

- `kuky_data/frequency_list_of_argmspans.rds`: a data frame of all spans from `argm.rds`, each span-relation on a separate column (unnested lists of links). 

-   `argumentativeSpanTextsMetadata.rds/.tsv`: produced by Chapter \@ref(chapter:first-preprocessing)
    
  - added span text derived from the offsets in the annotation and document metadata to each span. No links yet (at least not in an immediately usable form).
  
- `kuky_stoplight(.rds/.tsv)`: produced by Chapter \@ref(chapter:first-preprocessing)

 - added span text derived from the offsets in the annotation
 
- `kuky_argm_with_all_links_restored(.rds/.tsv)`: produced by Chapter \@ref(chapter:first-preprocessing)

 - integrated links in the ArgM annotation and automatically adding links between Conclusion and Rules when they shared a Narrative (as I planned it when I designed the annotation in Gloss to save annotators' effort). 
 
- `kuky_argm_total_links.rds/.tsv`: produced by Chapter \@ref(chapter:network-preprocessing)

 - added links between Conclusions that share common Narratives. 
 
 - I wanted to remove rows representing some spans as unlinked when they got linked during the processing, but it caused a partial data loss. I was not able to trace the problem, so I did not de-duplicate the future edges.
 
- `argm_vertices_df.rds/.tsv`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). Here I removed some columns irrelevant as machine-learning features. On the other hand, I added a few features concerning the lengths and positions of the span texts, including tokenization and sentence chunking. ArgM annotation only. 

- `argm_edges_df.rds/.tsv`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). I de-duplicated the edges between vertices that just swapped order. ArgM annotation only. 

`argm_vertices_stoplight_enriched_df.rds/.tsv`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). I added three columns: `Relevant`, `Superfluous`, and `Incomprehensible`. These are Stoplight labels. The values inside these columns is the proportion of the given ArgM span that pertains to this label. By this, I incorporated the Stoplight annotation directly into ArgM. Most ArgM spans are linked to only one Stoplight label, so the proportion is 1.00. 
 
- `vertices_list.rds`,  `edges_list.rds`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). Edges and vertices as data frames ready to go into `igraph`. Each document is going to have its own `igraph` object defined by a pair of vertices and edges data frames. For this, I have created a list of vertices data frames and a list of edges data frames. Both lists are named with identical names that encode the document and the annotation owner. (Mind that some documents have multiple annotation and I am still keeping all options available.) I used the `argm_vertices_stoplight_enriched_df` vertices and `argm_edges` to created these objects. s

- `igraphs.rds`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). A list of `igraph` objects of individual document-owner pairs. 

- `igraphs_sorted.rds`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). A list of `igraph` objects of individual document-owner pairs sorted by the initial character position of the span text (offset start, variable `start`). 

- `stoplight_vertices_df.rds/.tsv`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). A data frame of vertices of the stoplight annotation. 

- `stoplight_edges_df.rds/.tsv`: created in Chapter \ref@(chapter:network-analysis). A data frame of edges between the stoplight annotation spans and ArgM annotation spans.
